headline: The first official same-point comparison is in: Florida's returned mail ballots are D+6.7 by registration, against D+5.8 at this point in 2024, a year Republicans carried the state by 13. Elsewhere every measure is more Democratic than 2024 (Ohio's early electorate has gone from 36% Republican to 41% Democratic), while against 2022 mail volume is down in Wisconsin and North Carolina and Georgia's in-person turnout is running 40% ahead. Democrats have moved from mail to voting in person, which bends every comparison.

measures.label: Iowa: Democratic share of mail-ballot requests
measures.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; Catalist is a Democratic-aligned data vendor

measures.label: Pennsylvania: Democratic share of mail-ballot requests
measures.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; Catalist is a Democratic-aligned data vendor

measures.label: Maine: Democratic share of mail-ballot requests
measures.aff: Nonpartisan outlet; Catalist is a Democratic-aligned data vendor

measures.label: Virginia: Democratic share of early voters, two-party (L2 modeled party)
measures.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor; Virginia has no party registration, so party is modeled in both years

measures.label: Ohio: early voters by party (last primary ballot), D-minus-R margin
measures.src: News 5 Cleveland, Oct 13 (Ohio Secretary of State data)

compare_note: Democratic share of mail-ballot requests (CNN/Catalist, Oct 1). Gray dot is the same point in 2024. Virginia's early voters are 63% Democratic on L2's modeled two-party split, vs. 59% at the same point in 2024 (Morris, Oct 12); Ohio's early voters were 41% Democratic and 28% Republican by last primary ballot as of Oct 13, vs. 26% and 36% at this point in 2024 (News 5 Cleveland, from Secretary of State data). Florida's, Nevada's, Colorado's, Iowa's, Pennsylvania's and North Carolina's comparisons are computed from the official files. CNN also found that the 2022 request pools were more Democratic than 2026's in every listed state except Iowa.

bullets.title: Georgia's in-person voting is running 40% ahead of 2022.
bullets.html: The Secretary of State counted 188,667 in-person voters on Oct 13, against 134,962 on the first day of 2022 and 70,849 in 2018; after two days the total was nearly 365,000 in person plus more than 16,000 accepted absentee ballots. Mail is small (10,267 accepted on day one). Of the first day's ballots, 54% came from voters 65 and over, 37% from Black voters and 50% from white voters; 79% had voted early in 2022.
bullets.aff: Official data; GeorgiaVotes is an independent tracker of the state's files

bullets.title: Ohio's early electorate has flipped from Republican to Democratic.
bullets.html: Of nearly 230,000 early votes as of Oct 13, about 95,000 came from Democrats (41%), 67,000 from unaffiliated voters and nearly 64,000 from Republicans (28%), by last primary ballot; at this point in 2024 Republicans were 36% and Democrats 26%. In the 81 counties Trump carried, both parties are at 39%, vs. 20% Democratic and 44% Republican a week in two years ago. The official count through Oct 13 was 194,841 in-person votes (50,368 at the same point in 2022) and 33,629 mail ballots returned, with requests at about 631,000 vs. 871,041 then.
bullets.aff: Official data via a nonpartisan outlet

bullets.title: The edge over 2024 is real but partly a change in how Democrats vote.
bullets.html: Democratic mail requests in North Carolina are down 40% from 2022, against 18% for Republicans, yet Democrats are returning ballots faster (22% returned vs. 17% in 2022). In Pennsylvania, 30% of the Democrats who had voted early by this point in 2024 have already voted again, vs. 18% of Republicans (L2 data via G. Elliott Morris). In an NBC poll, 23% of Democrats plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in 2024, and 36% plan to vote early in person, up from 30%.
bullets.aff: Nonpartisan; L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor

bullets.title: Wisconsin's mail vote is down 30% on 2022; Michigan's has flattened.
bullets.html: Wisconsin clerks had received about 128,000 absentee ballots three weeks out, against nearly 184,000 at the same point in 2022; Madison fell from about 31,700 to about 9,000, which Dane County's clerk attributes to distrust of the Postal Service. Michigan's returned absentee ballots (440,677 on Oct 13) are only slightly above the same point in 2022 (432,960), though requests are up more than 20% because of the permanent mail list. Neither state registers voters by party.

bullets.title: Florida's mail vote is a shade more Democratic than at this point in 2024.
bullets.html: By registration, 669,634 returned mail ballots were D+6.7 as of Oct 14 (286,869 Democrats, 241,910 Republicans, 140,855 others); at the same point in 2024, 709,359 ballots were D+5.8 (303,597 to 262,136). Republicans erased the Democratic mail lead once in-person voting opened in both 2022 and 2024; it opens Oct 19 this year, and about 1.77 million mail ballots are still out.
sources: Florida Division of Elections via the app's official comparison, Oct 14

bullets.title: Democratic data firms report a Latino and Black surge.
bullets.html: TargetSmart's Tom Bonier says the Hispanic share of the early vote is above the same point in 2022 in more than 94% of 229 comparable counties, with about 112,000 Latino early votes vs. 106,000 at this point in 2024. No independent replication yet.

bullets.title: Republicans say they vote later.
bullets.html: National Review's Noah Rothman argues Democrats will lead the early vote, "but perhaps not by the margins the party expects," because their own warnings eroded trust in mail. Ohio Republican strategist Bob Clegg says early voting "really tells you nothing" because Republicans vote later, while acknowledging a turnout problem. Wisconsin's GOP reads the Madison and Milwaukee declines as "a lack of enthusiasm among Dem voters." No quantitative RNC early-vote claims for 2026 turned up.
bullets.aff: GOP-aligned claims, reported by nonpartisan outlets

bullets.title: Nevada is the cautionary tale.
bullets.html: Nearly 14,000 mail ballots had been accepted by the evening of Oct 14, about 0.7% of active voters, with Democrats about 1,200 ballots (9 points) ahead statewide; Clark County is 65% of the vote and Democrats lead it by about 12. Jon Ralston says it is "way too early to draw any conclusions." In-person voting starts Oct 17; in 2024 Democrats led the mail vote, Republicans led the total early vote, and Trump won.

calendar_note: North Carolina's one-stop voting opened Oct 15; Georgia's in-person voting opened Oct 13; Iowa and Kansas mail ballots went out Oct 14. Colorado mailed its ballots Oct 2-9; Oct 19 is when its voter service centers must open. Pennsylvania and New Hampshire have no early in-person voting.
cast_at_note: Ballots counted (UF Election Lab, 38 jurisdictions reporting, state data as of Oct 9-15) when these comparisons were compiled; sets the automatic early-vote weight.
signals_verdict: The first official same-point comparison, Florida's, is close to 2024: returned mail ballots are D+6.7 by registration vs. D+5.8 at this point two years ago, when Republicans went on to carry the state by 13; the other five states' 2022 and 2024 baselines begin 12-19 days out, so their comparisons arrive over the coming week. Elsewhere the early vote is more Democratic than 2024 wherever it can be measured (Ohio's early voters have gone from 36% Republican and 26% Democratic to 41% Democratic and 28% Republican), while against 2022 mail volume is down in Wisconsin and North Carolina and Georgia's in-person turnout is up 40%; all of it is bent by Democrats moving from mail to in person, so the early vote is consistent with the polls rather than ahead of them. The next tests are North Carolina's first one-stop day, Nevada's in-person start on Oct 17 and Florida's on Oct 19.

signals.title: Georgia's first day of in-person voting ran well ahead of 2022
signals.value: 188,667 in-person votes on Oct 13 vs. 134,962 on the first day of 2022 (70,849 in 2018), per the Secretary of State; nearly 365,000 in person after two days, plus more than 16,000 accepted absentee ballots. About 130,000 mail ballots requested vs. nearly 286,000 by the end of 2022.
signals.catch: Georgia has no party registration, so this is turnout, not direction. Part of the in-person surge is voters who would have used mail; the 2024 first day was over 300,000.
signals.src: Georgia Secretary of State, Oct 14; FOX 5 Atlanta, Oct 15

signals.title: Ohio's early electorate has flipped from Republican to Democratic
signals.value: As of Oct 13, Democrats were 41% of nearly 230,000 early votes (about 95,000) and Republicans 28% (nearly 64,000), by last primary ballot; at this point in 2024 Republicans were 36% and Democrats 26%. In the 81 Trump counties both parties are at 39%, vs. D 20% and R 44% then. Official count through Oct 13: 194,841 in person (50,368 at the same point in 2022).
signals.catch: 2024 was a presidential year, and Ohio Republicans are shifting from mail to later voting: mail requests are about 631,000 vs. 871,041 at this point in 2022. 'Party' is the last primary ballot pulled.
signals.src: News 5 Cleveland (Ohio Secretary of State data), Oct 13

signals.title: Virginia's early voters lean further Democratic than in 2024
signals.value: 63% Democratic on L2's modeled two-party split, vs. 59% at the same point in 2024 (378,000 D to 265,000 R then). 46% of 2024's Democratic early voters have already voted again, vs. 35% of Republicans. CNN/Catalist (Oct 1): voters with only Democratic primary history lead those with only GOP history by 18 points, vs. 8 in 2024.
signals.catch: Virginia has no party registration, so party is modeled, and 2024 had a presidential-year electorate.
signals.src: G. Elliott Morris (L2 data), Oct 12; CNN/Catalist, Oct 1
signals.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor; Catalist is a Democratic-aligned vendor

signals.title: Democrats are returning their ballots faster than in 2022
signals.value: North Carolina: 22% of Democrats' requested ballots are back, vs. 17% at this point in 2022. Pennsylvania: 20% vs. 15%.
signals.catch: It could be enthusiasm, or worry that the mail will be slow; NBC/Penn say the data can't tell yet.

signals.title: Pennsylvania's 2024 Democratic early voters are coming back faster
signals.value: 30% of the Democrats who had voted early by this point in 2024 have already voted, vs. 18% of Republicans; of about 153,000 matched early voters, 76% are registered Democrats and 17% Republicans, vs. 66% and 25% at the same point in 2024.
signals.catch: L2's match covers less than half of the 346,932 ballots the state had counted by Oct 14; the official comparison (above) will supersede the party shares once the 2024 baseline reaches this point. Pennsylvania's mail vote is lopsidedly Democratic every year.
signals.aff: L2 is a nonpartisan commercial vendor

signals.title: Democrats' share of mail requests is up from 2024
signals.value: Iowa 67% vs. 54% at the same point in 2024; North Carolina 42% vs. 36%; Pennsylvania 66% vs. 62%; Maine 57% vs. 53%.
signals.catch: Against 2022 the same shares are lower everywhere except Iowa (see the other column).

signals.title: Trump country in New Jersey is voting less Republican
signals.value: In counties Trump won by 20+, the pre-election vote has shifted nearly 11 points toward Democrats vs. this point in 2024.
signals.catch: Small counties and a presidential-year baseline.

signals.title: Wisconsin's mail vote is running 30% behind 2022
signals.value: About 128,000 absentee ballots returned three weeks out, vs. nearly 184,000 at the same point in 2022. Madison: about 9,000 vs. about 31,700.
signals.catch: No party registration; the Dane County clerk blames distrust of the Postal Service, and in-person absentee voting doesn't start until Oct 20.
signals.src: WPR, using Wisconsin Elections Commission data, Oct 13

signals.title: Michigan's mail returns have fallen back to the 2022 pace
signals.value: 440,677 ballots returned by Oct 13, vs. 432,960 at the same point in 2022; a week earlier returns were 30% ahead. Requests are up more than 20% (2,083,240 vs. 1,707,970).
signals.catch: Michigan has no party registration, so this measures turnout, not direction. About 95% of requests come from the permanent mail list; in-person early voting opens Oct 24.

signals.title: Against 2022, Democrats' share of mail requests is down
signals.value: Lower now than at this point in 2022 in every state CNN checked except Iowa.
signals.catch: Democrats are moving from mail to early in-person voting: 23% plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in 2024 (NBC poll).

signals.title: North Carolina Democrats requested far fewer mail ballots
signals.value: Requests vs. the same point in 2022: Democrats down 42%, Republicans down 19%.
signals.catch: Same mode shift. North Carolina's in-person early voting, where most of its vote is cast, starts Oct 15.

signals.title: Pennsylvania Republicans are requesting more mail ballots
signals.value: Requests vs. the same point in 2022: Republicans up 18%, Democrats down 14%.
signals.catch: Republicans have been urged to vote by mail this year, so more requests may be a change of method rather than more voters.

signals.title: Georgia's mail requests fell more in Democratic areas
signals.value: Down 52% in heavily Harris precincts vs. 39% in heavily Trump precincts.
signals.catch: Mail is about 5% of Georgia's vote; the first day of in-person voting (Oct 13) ran well ahead of 2022.
